goals.text: Consolidate the web app and shared UI package into one workspace.
Cut CI time with affected-only builds and cached task outputs.
Share a typed UI package without allowing apps to become package dependencies.

audience.text: Product engineers working in apps/web daily.
Platform maintainers who own packages/ui and build tooling.
Release managers who need predictable package versioning.

constraints.text: pnpm workspaces with Turborepo task orchestration.
One lockfile, one root tsconfig, one root CI workflow.

assumptions.text: Packages can build in isolation once dependencies are declared correctly.
Remote cache access is available in CI but not required locally.

risks.text: Cross-package relative imports could bypass the declared graph.
Circular dependencies may appear during migration.

repoConventions.text: TypeScript strict mode is on. Never use `any`; prefer `unknown` + narrow at the boundary.

uxRules.text: `tsconfig.json` at the repo root defines shared compiler options; package tsconfigs extend it and only add overrides.
Naming: `@scope/utils`, `@scope/ui`, `@scope/config`. The scope prefix makes internal-vs-external explicit in every import.
Each package has its own README explaining what it exports and the boundary with the rest of the repo.

a11yRules.text: All interactive elements must be reachable and operable with the keyboard alone.
Focus must be visible at all times; never remove outlines without replacing them.
Text contrast must meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text).
Every form control has a programmatic label.
Pages use proper landmark regions (header, main, nav, footer) and a sensible heading order.

componentGuidance.text: packages/* — internal libraries. Private by default; each exports a typed public surface via index.ts.
apps/* — deployable targets. Depend on packages/, never the other way around.
tools/* — repo-local scripts, codegens, CI helpers. Not published.
BuildGraph — one root config (turbo.json, nx.json, or a root package.json scripts map) that declares task deps. Every script is reproducible from a clean clone.
ChangeGate — affected-package detection for CI: only run the build / test / lint for packages that actually changed (or depend on a change).

qaGuardrails.text: Unit tests live next to source as `*.test.ts`. Run `vitest run` in CI and before every commit touching business logic.
Success criterion to verify before launch: Every workspace builds and tests in isolation.
Success criterion to verify before launch: A no-op PR finishes affected-only CI in under 60 seconds.
Success criterion to verify before launch: Release flow uses changesets; no manual package version bumps.
Every package compiles in isolation: `cd packages/<name> && npm run build` succeeds without repo-root tooling on PATH.
Cross-package imports go through the package name, not a relative ../../../../ path.
CI uses affected-only runs and caches build artefacts. A no-op PR finishes in under 60s.
Every publishable package has a CHANGELOG.md updated via changesets or equivalent — never hand-edited in the release commit.
Version bumps flow through a single tool (changesets / lerna / nx release) — no manual `npm version` in a package.
Lockfile is a single source of truth (pnpm-lock.yaml or package-lock.json). No per-package lockfiles.

dosAndDonts.text: Prefer small, focused diffs. One concern per PR or patch.
Always show the exact test or typecheck command you ran and its result.
When following a rule from this file, cite it by section heading so reviewers can audit.
Do not refactor code unrelated to the task, even if it looks better.
Do not add new dependencies without flagging the choice and reason.
When adding a new package, use the repo's generator / template if one exists. If not, copy the smallest existing package wholesale and edit from there.
Declare dependencies explicitly in each package's package.json — hoisting works, but the declared graph is what CI trusts.
Keep the build graph DAG: packages/* never import from apps/*.
Do not add a global helper in the repo root. It belongs in a package.
Do not cross-reference packages with relative paths (`../../../other-package`). Use the package name so the build graph is honest.
Do not mix ESM and CommonJS within a single package. Pick one per package and stick to it.

unsafeActions.text: Never modify generated files (anything under `dist/`, `build/`, `.next/`, or marked `@generated`).
Never commit secrets. Redact any `.env*` content that appears in logs or diffs.
Never hand-edit generated files in `dist/` or `.turbo/` or `.nx/` — they get blown away on the next build.
Never bypass the changeset / release tool to publish a package manually; that's how versions diverge from the changelog.

responseExpectations.text: Before claiming work is complete, run the repo's typecheck and test commands and show the output.
If the brief is ambiguous on a specific section, ask rather than guess. Cite the section heading.

components.text: Feature components live co-located with the route or feature folder that owns them.

sprint1.text: Commit the Project Spine–generated `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and `.cursor/rules/project-spine.mdc` after review.
Pick and configure a linter (Biome or ESLint) with a minimal rule set.
Deliver: Consolidate the web app and shared UI package into one workspace.
Deliver: Cut CI time with affected-only builds and cached task outputs.
Deliver: Share a typed UI package without allowing apps to become package dependencies.
